_recapture_log.delta: OFF/ON standalone action ceilings only, three modules that had no entry and were therefore held at an implicit zero: package_environment 0->2, cli_bootstrap_array_core 0->106, py_frontend.compiled_owned_passes 0->30. _recapture_log.reason: These are cross-module call actions, not libpython links. package_environment and cli_bootstrap_array_core already carried theirs before this change; they are recorded here rather than left as an implicit zero that reports every run as a fresh regression. compiled_owned_passes went 26->30 when `mem2reg` was routed to the owned pcc/native_ir kernel, which is the change that took the runtime archive from 17218 allocas to 1730 and the gateway from 24890 to 38747 QPS; the dispatcher already imported five native_ir modules the same way, so this is a sixth instance of an existing shape, not a new one. The underlying gap is one capability: a call into another module of the closure lowers to a getattr bridge instead of a direct call. Measured consequences elsewhere: importing three shared helpers into cli_bootstrap costs 84 such calls, which is why the host CLI and the bootstrap CLI still keep separate copies, and why the C driver is reached through a child process. Closing that gap removes these three entries and unblocks a single CLI implementation; it is recorded in docs/investigations/runtime-module-optimizer-throughput.md.
